scores.accuracy_concern: Verify the figures (about 227 falls in 130 residents; weight shifting about 41%, trip or stumble about 21%) and note that cameras were in common areas, not bedrooms or bathrooms; the position on transfers is an inference, not a tested intervention.
scores.sharpen: Mark the recommendation on transfers and sitting down as judgement drawn from the finding, and state the camera limitation on the chart itself.

scores.accuracy_concern: MDS PSP criteria specify repeated unprovoked falls within 3 years of onset; 'backward' is characteristic but is not in the criterion wording; the NPH gait description and shunt response should be worded from the Relkin or Nakajima guideline.
scores.sharpen: Match each carousel label word for word to the cited criteria and cut to three vignettes if four cannot be read at phone size.

scores.accuracy_concern: Verify Lundin-Olsson 1997 numbers (58 residents in Umea; 12 stopped walking; 10 of 12 fell within six months, compared with about 11 of 46) and the Beauchet 2009 sensitivity and specificity conclusions.
scores.sharpen: End with the plain rule on weight: a positive sign means look harder, a negative sign does not reassure.

scores.values_concern: Mention comfort, continence and dressing as reasons people stop wearing them without implying residents are non-compliant.
scores.accuracy_concern: Cochrane 2014 figures (nursing care RR about 0.82, about 11 fewer hip fractures per 1000, moderate certainty; community little or no effect) must be copied exactly; the pelvic fracture signal is uncertain and should be omitted or stated as uncertain.
scores.sharpen: Use a 100-person or 1000-person icon array that stays legible at phone size, and open with the absolute number rather than the description of the garment.

scores.accuracy_concern: Middle meningeal artery embolisation is now used as an adjunct after 2024 trials; avoid implying surgical drainage is the only treatment, and say 'often treatable' rather than 'treatable'.
scores.sharpen: Keep the timeline card and add the one sentence families most need: the knock may have seemed too minor to mention, so mention it anyway.

scores.accuracy_concern: VISIBLE overall result did not show a clear difference; the benefit in the regular-outdoor-activity subgroup and the increase in outdoor falls in the low-outdoor-activity group must be stated as a planned subgroup result with direction and size verified.
scores.sharpen: Lead the second slide with the overall null result and then the two subgroups, and allocate to C01 or C14, not both.

scores.accuracy_concern: Absolute figures must come from the Cochrane summary of findings table (rate ratio about 0.77, risk ratio about 0.85; per-1000 figures to verify); the two outcomes use different denominators (person-years and people), and 'what one person can expect' needs careful wording because neither figure predicts for an individual.
scores.sharpen: Open with the two numbers from the same review side by side, so the reader sees the gap before the explanation.

scores.accuracy_concern: Tinetti 1993 is a 1993 New Haven cohort (about half of non-injured fallers could not get up unaided; verify); evidence that practising reduces long lies comes from small studies, so the post should say practice builds confidence and skill, not that it prevents long lies; the carousel must tell people with pain or suspected injury not to try.
scores.sharpen: Pair the getting-up carousel with one slide from C01-21 on what to do if you can't, so the set covers both outcomes on the floor.

scores.values_concern: Make clear that seated exercise has other benefits and can be a start for people who can't yet stand for long, so frailer readers are not told their class is worthless.
scores.accuracy_concern: 'Seated exercise has not been shown to reduce falls' must match Sherrington's wording; the 3 hours a week and high balance challenge finding comes from meta-regression across trials, not a trial of dose.
scores.sharpen: Keep the four questions but add one line on what to do if no such class exists locally (ask about a home-based programme such as Otago).

scores.values_concern: Keep the criticism on the metric and the incentive it creates, not on ward nurses or managers as a group.
scores.accuracy_concern: There is no direct evidence here that wards lower falls rates by immobilising people; present it as a limitation of the metric (judgement), and give Brown 2009's time-in-bed figure as one US hospital cohort.
scores.sharpen: Name one specific mobility measure a ward can report next to falls per 1000 bed days, and cite a service or audit that already does so.

scores.accuracy_concern: Group names and proportions from Delbaere 2010 (vigorous, anxious, stoic, aware) and which group had which associations must be verified; one Sydney cohort of people aged 70 to 90.
scores.sharpen: Put the grid first and give one plain sentence per cell on the help that fits, and keep the percentages only if they come straight from the paper.

scores.accuracy_concern: Verify the Wild, Nayak and Isaacs 1981 sample size and recruitment and that the 'half died within six months' figure refers only to those who lay more than an hour; do not imply the figure is wrong, only that it is small and associational; check which outcomes Fleming 2008 linked with long lies.
scores.sharpen: State in the first two lines what the check found (small, old and associational, but newer cohorts still point the same way) so the post does not read as a concealed answer.
Add what to do with the answer (tell the GP or physiotherapist, ask about a strength and balance programme and help with the activity itself), so the question leads somewhere beyond E076.

scores.accuracy_concern: Cummings 1988 reported the share of people with a confirmed fall who did not recall falling at 12 months (about 13 to 32% depending on how they were asked), not the share of falls forgotten; the opening line must be corrected.
scores.sharpen: Fix the opening statistic to people rather than falls, and make the diary template printable with the column for 'could you get up' kept.

scores.accuracy_concern: The ISTUMBLE items must be quoted exactly from the current ambulance service version; the first-aid and HSE sources are web pages that could not be opened from this environment, and safety-critical wording needs an opened document source.
scores.sharpen: Take the checklist verbatim from one opened, current source and keep the head-knock-on-a-blood-thinner item here, so that C01-07 can be dropped or merged.

scores.accuracy_concern: Butt 2012 measured hip fracture, not falls, and reported a relative increase (about 40% in the first 45 days, verify) from observational data; give the absolute risk and use association wording.
scores.sharpen: Make the onset date the single instruction and show one worked, labelled illustrative timeline, so it reads as a history-taking method rather than a repeat of E066.

scores.accuracy_concern: 'No agreed clinical definition' needs a citable source; trip biomechanics come mainly from laboratory studies of healthy older adults (Pavol 2001), so avoid overstating how they apply to a frail 85-year-old.
scores.sharpen: Give the replacement note in full (for example: tripped on threshold, did not lose consciousness, lying and standing BP done, gait observed) so the reader leaves with wording to copy.

scores.accuracy_concern: NICE CG179 does not give a time frame for pressure damage on a hard surface; use 'can include' for the complications list and avoid a precise hour threshold unless sourced.
scores.sharpen: Add the practical point that 'time on the floor' is often an estimate, and record the last time seen well alongside it, as the post already hints.

scores.accuracy_concern: Kendrick 2014 found a small to moderate effect immediately after exercise with low-certainty evidence for longer-term effects; say so, and note that CBT-based programmes are not widely available in the UK.
scores.sharpen: Open with the treatment rather than the questionnaire, and say where a practitioner can refer or what they can start themselves.

scores.values_concern: Frame rails as a question of liberty as well as safety, and avoid presenting a restless person as a problem to contain.
scores.accuracy_concern: Healey 2008 conclusions must be quoted precisely; MHRA guidance date and the restraint framing differ between UK nations (Care Inspectorate in Scotland, CQC in England).
scores.sharpen: Add the two questions families can ask the ward or home (might they roll out, will they try to climb over), which is what the post's argument turns on.

scores.values_concern: Treat 'not wanting to trouble anyone' respectfully, as a reasonable feeling to plan around, not a failing.
scores.accuracy_concern: Fleming 2008 studied people aged 90 and over in Cambridge; the non-use figure must be stated with that population and denominator (falls when alone and unable to get up among people who had an alarm).
scores.sharpen: Add the specific agreement to make in advance ('any time on the floor, press it') as the closing instruction and check whether automatic fall detectors need a sentence.

scores.accuracy_concern: The wrist-crease height rule and the share of aids set at the wrong height rest on patient guidance and small studies; avoid implying frames cause falls rather than demanding attention and both hands.
scores.sharpen: Allocate to C02 or here, not both, and give the three home checks in the order a family would do them on the first day.

scores.accuracy_concern: The explanation that mixed results are 'partly because withdrawal doesn't happen or last' is inference; Campbell 1999 had 93 participants and restarting was measured after the trial; IMPROveFALL withdrawal rates and the Lee 2021 pooled result need verifying.
scores.sharpen: Present the follow-through problem as a plausible explanation marked as such, and give the one practical step (check at a set interval that the stopped medicine has stayed stopped); allocate to C01 or C06.

scores.values_concern: Present families' protective restriction with sympathy and keep the older person as the decision-maker without casting relatives as the problem.
scores.accuracy_concern: Deshpande 2008 is observational: say activity restriction is linked with later decline in function rather than that giving up activities reduces strength and balance.
scores.sharpen: Merge with C01-13 or give it a distinct test, such as one named activity worked through from 'what makes it risky' to 'what can change'.

scores.accuracy_concern: Brown 2000 studied women only, and the link is an association; there is no trial evidence here that treating urgency reduces falls, and antimuscarinic bladder drugs can themselves raise falls risk.
scores.sharpen: Say plainly that treating urgency is worth doing for its own sake and that trials have not shown it prevents falls; allocate to C01 or C12.

scores.accuracy_concern: NICE NG232 wording for anticoagulated people with no other CT indication must be checked ('consider' or 'perform' a CT within 8 hours, and whether antiplatelet monotherapy is excluded); 'recommends a scan even when they seem well' may overstate the guidance.
scores.sharpen: Merge into C01-06 or C01-28, since the single fact it carries appears in both of those posts.

scores.accuracy_concern: The World Falls Guidelines 2022 put a single non-injurious fall in an intermediate group (gait and balance check first), not straight into multifactorial assessment; 'whether or not there was an injury' must match the exact NICE NG249 criteria, and later ED-based trials after PROFET were mixed.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the evidence on further falls after an ED attendance and give the GP two or three things to do this week, rather than a general list that echoes E067 and E079.

scores.accuracy_concern: The NHS advice wording (for example, changing position about every 30 minutes) comes from web pages that could not be opened here; verify from an opened document before quoting.
scores.sharpen: Merge with C01-03 as the 'if you can't get up' slide, or give it a stronger opening that names the preparation to do today (phone in a pocket, a throw at floor level).

scores.accuracy_concern: SAFER 2 did not show a clear difference in its primary outcomes and referral uptake was low, and non-conveyance rates vary widely between services; the post must not imply that ambulance referral pathways are proven to reduce falls.
scores.sharpen: Keep one handover post (this or C01-01), and give the reader the exact words to ask the crew and a named route (GP or local falls service) if they forget.

scores.accuracy_concern: Naseri 2018 found benefit mainly for home hazard modification in people with a falls history after discharge, and did not show clear benefit for post-discharge exercise or medication review; the claim that all three steps 'have evidence behind them' in that window overclaims.
scores.sharpen: Narrow it to the one post-discharge intervention with trial support (occupational therapy home hazard work for people who have fallen, or the Safe Recovery education trial) and say plainly what is less certain.

scores.accuracy_concern: Evidence that community classes reach fewer of the poorest people may be thin: Nyman and Victor 2012 addresses participation factors rather than socioeconomic reach; Liu-Ambrose 2019 effect size to verify.
scores.sharpen: Find a source that measures who takes up classes by deprivation or housebound status; without it the post repeats E083's call for home-based programmes.

allocation_reason: 29 of 31 candidates reach 36 or more with no disqualifying flag, and even after collapsing internal clusters (floor and long lie, fear of falling, head injury, handover) and setting aside the four that belong equally to C02, C06, C12 or C14, more than 14 distinct strong posts remain.
balance_note: The top 14 by score are 6 practitioner (18, 27, 24, 02, 05, 08), 4 public (28, 03, 25, 31) and 4 both (14, 23, 19, 13), so public and carer coverage is adequate but thinner than practitioner; Reading the evidence is over-represented (02, 08, 18, 19, 24) and Care that works is absent, so consider swapping 08 or 02 for 06 (carers deciding on the floor) or 20. Avoid pairing 03 with 21, 13 with 09, or 06 with 07, and keep 23, 26, 30 and 11 in one category only.
notes: The stated formula 2U+2A+2D+S+F+1.5N+1.5E has a true maximum of 55, not 50; totals here follow the formula as written. No candidate is about delirium.
